name: A crossing
why: 1: they cross at (2, 2). C and D are on opposite sides of AB, and A and B on opposite sides of CD.

name: Apart
why: 0. C and D are on the same side of AB.

name: The lines cross, the pieces do not
why: 0. The two lines meet at (1.5, 1.5), past the end of both pieces. A and B are on the same side of CD.

name: Parallel
why: 0: the pieces are parallel, 1 apart. C and D are on the same side of AB.

name: Touching ends
why: 1: they share the end (2, 2). An orientation of 0 needs the extra check that the point lies on the other piece.

name: An end on the middle
why: 1: the piece CD stands on AB at (2, 0).

name: Almost touching
why: 0. C is 1 above AB, so its orientation is not 0, and the piece CD does not reach down to AB.

name: On one line, apart
why: 0. All four orientations are 0, but the pieces do not overlap. An answer that says 'all on one line, so they meet' fails here.

name: On one line, end to end
On one line, overlapping
why: 2: they share the whole piece from (1, 1) to (3, 3).

name: One inside the other
why: 2: the piece from (2, 0) to (3, 0) lies inside the other, so they share all of it.

name: Upright and overlapping
why: 2. On an upright line all x are equal, so compare the y values.

name: Upright and apart
why: 0. Comparing only the x values would say they overlap.

name: A single point on a piece
why: 1. A piece may be a single point (both ends equal).

name: A point off the line
why: 0: the single point (1, 2) is not on the line through (0, 0) and (2, 3): its cross product is 2 × 2 − 3 × 1 = 1, not 0.

name: Far from floats
why: 0. The point is 1 part in 10³⁴ off the line: its cross product is exactly 1. With floats both products round to 10³⁴ and the point seems to lie on the piece. Python's whole numbers are exact.
